outcome: Prevalence of intermittent absent or reversed end-diastolic flow (iAREDF) in the umbilical artery
Pregnancy outcome (fetal death, brain damage in co-twin, early premature emergency section for fetal distress)
cohort: The study participants were appropriately grown monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) pregnancies, divided into those with and without proximate cord insertion.
finding: Intermittent absent or reversed end-diastolic flow (iAREDF) was significantly more prevalent in monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) pregnancies with proximate cord insertion (PCI) compared to those without, correlating with a larger diameter of arterioarterial (AA) anastomoses and an increased risk for adverse pregnancy outcomes including fetal death and early premature emergency section.
